title: The Art of the Double Meaning
text:
Wordplay is the deliberate exploitation of ambiguity, where a single term carries two meanings at once. Puns are its most familiar form: a well-placed homophone can turn an ordinary remark into a sly joke. Skilled writers, however, rarely settle for mere cleverness; they use double meaning to reveal character, mock pretension, or quietly undermine what a speaker claims to believe.

Shakespeare offers countless examples, often letting a servant or fool exploit a word's secondary sense while the nobles remain oblivious. Translators face a particular dilemma here, since a pun that delights in one language frequently dies in transit. Consequently, many translators abandon the original joke and substitute a new one that produces a comparable effect in the target tongue.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what is a pun most commonly built on?
options: A homophone that turns a remark into a joke
A silent gesture rather than speech

questions.text: What does the second paragraph say a servant or fool often does in Shakespeare's plays?
Why would a translator probably replace a pun instead of translating it word for word?
options: The pun would lose its effect in the new language
The original pun was actually a mistake
Readers of the target language dislike jokes
Puns are forbidden in translated works

questions.text: What can be inferred about how skilled writers use double meaning?
options: They use it for more than simple amusement
They avoid it entirely in serious texts
They use it only to confuse their readers
They consider it a sign of weak writing

vocabulary.definition: the quality of having more than one possible meaning
a word that sounds like another but has a different meaning
a claim to importance or value that may not be justified
a difficult situation where every choice has a disadvantage

paragraph_translations: O trocadilho é a exploração deliberada da ambiguidade, em que um único termo carrega dois significados ao mesmo tempo. Os trocadilhos são sua forma mais conhecida: um homófono bem colocado pode transformar uma observação comum numa piada sagaz. Escritores habilidosos, porém, raramente se contentam com a mera esperteza; usam o duplo sentido para revelar caráter, ridicularizar a pretensão ou minar discretamente aquilo que um falante afirma acreditar.

Shakespeare oferece inúmeros exemplos, muitas vezes deixando que um criado ou um bobo explore o sentido secundário de uma palavra enquanto os nobres permanecem alheios. Os tradutores enfrentam aqui um dilema particular, pois um trocadilho que encanta numa língua frequentemente se perde na transposição. Consequentemente, muitos tradutores abandonam a piada original e a substituem por outra que produza um efeito comparável na língua de chegada.
